title: Ring tool crashes the scene on a quad mesh: 'intrinsic triangulation needs triangles' from RingTool.adoptGraphRings
description:
Found 2026-10-03 (VIEW-12 testing): loading a quad mesh (a copy of the staged finger model) in the ring-tool editing scene kills the scene with IllegalArgumentException 'intrinsic triangulation needs triangles', thrown from RingTool.adoptGraphRings (added by CRAW-35), which builds SurfaceGeodesics on the surface as loaded. The ring tool should work on any surface the viewer shows: triangulate a working copy for the geodesic engine (keeping a map back to the original faces for picking and drawing) or, if that is out of reach, refuse with a clear message in the log and leave the scene running. Never crash the scene.

Rework 2026-10-03 (user decision): spline_ring must pass the input mesh through unchanged (quads stay quads; recovering quads from triangles downstream is expensive). It traces on an internal TriangulatedCopy as now, but its output geometry is the original mesh, and the ring's edge mask is snapped onto the original mesh's edges only (no diagonals), so ring_regions and later statements see the user's mesh. The traced spline it carries (CRAW-37's _surface_splines slot, if CRAW-37 has landed) keeps its crossings on the triangulated copy together with whatever the cut-out needs to map back. The editing scene's tools keep working on the triangulated copy for picking and tracing. Reload of a saved ring on a quad graph gives the same marks.

Rework 3, 2026-10-03 (user review): TriangulatedCopy is a hack that duplicates an existing layer. IntrinsicTriangulation.over(mesh) already builds its own connectivity mirroring the source mesh with sourceMesh and sourceFaceId maps, and FlipOut already creates intrinsic edges with no source counterpart; the only thing stopping quads is the triangles-only check in IntrinsicTriangulation.buildConnectivity. Move polygon handling there: buildConnectivity splits each polygon into intrinsic triangles (quads on the shorter diagonal, larger polygons fanned or ear-split), the split edges are intrinsic edges with no source edge (lengths from source positions), and sourceFaceId maps each intrinsic triangle to its source polygon. Results reach the user's mesh through the existing source maps: a traced point on a split edge is a point inside its source face, and ring masks snap onto source edges only. Then delete TriangulatedCopy and everything that exists to carry it: the RingScene.halfEdgeSurface override and markedSurface/ringMaskSurface, SurfaceSpline.edgeMesh and the two-mesh snap, RingRegionExtraction's triangle-to-source-face map and cutSurface. spline_ring passes its mesh through because nothing replaces it.
definition-of-done:
1. Loading a quad mesh in the editing scene does not crash; the ring tool either works on it (preferred) or reports why not. 2. A ring drawn on a quad mesh saves and reloads, if supported. 3. Unit test on a procedural quad mesh.

R1. On a quad graph, the output of spline_ring has the same face count and face arity as its input (unit test), and its ring mask marks only original edges forming a closed loop. R2. Save and reload on the quad tube and finger copies give identical ring fingerprints. R3. ring_regions on a quad graph with a ring splits it as before; the region tool still works in the scene.

R4. TriangulatedCopy no longer exists; RingScene.halfEdgeSurface is not overridden; SurfaceSpline references one mesh. R5. IntrinsicTriangulation.over accepts quads and mixed polygons (unit test: geodesic on a quad grid equals the analytic one; sourceFaceId covers every intrinsic triangle). R6. All earlier CRAW-39 and CRAW-37 tests and the fertility/tube numbers still hold.
testing-plan: 1. Unit test: adoptGraphRings on a procedural quad cylinder. 2. F5 the editing scene and switch to a quad model from the menu.
changes-made: Approach: RingScene.halfEdgeSurface() now hands every editing tool (ring, region, orbit, rings/ui-state routes) a triangle copy of a polygon mesh built by the new TriangulatedCopy (quads split on the shorter diagonal, larger polygons fanned), which keeps every vertex id, edge id/direction and the active vertex and edge order of the shown mesh, so graph ring marks, anchor vertex ids, saved anchor positions, the region tool's per-vertex tags and anchor discs need no mapping; diagonals get new edge ids. spline_ring triangulates its input the same way (outputting the triangle bundle), so a ring saved on a quad graph reloads. RingTool builds SurfaceGeodesics through readyGeodesics(), which on any failure logs '[ring-tool] the ring tool cannot trace rings on this surface: ...' and leaves the scene running.

Verified 2026-10-03: QuadRingToolTest (procedural quad cylinder with 16-gon caps: copy keeps ids/order/positions; adoptGraphRings gives the quad ring anchors; a saved spline_ring reloads on the quad mesh element-exact); mvn test 367 run, 0 failures; wt done build + launch OK. In app on tmp copies (tmp/quad_finger.dsl from test_finger, tmp/quad_tube.dsl from varying_tube_test): scene no longer crashes (log: triangle copy 564 triangles from 288 faces / 2528 from 1280), drafted + confirmed + Ctrl+S saved a ring, relaunch reloaded it with the same fingerprint (finger b4af3071a82c3470, tube 2e64abc9f991b230), Ctrl+T region tool split the tube into 2 regions and selected one. Screenshots tmp/craw39-tube-draft.png, -confirmed.png, -regions.png, -reloaded.png. fertility_rings.dsl untouched.

Rework 2026-10-03 (quads stay quads): spline_ring now passes its input mesh through unchanged (half-edge form, same face count and arity) and traces on an internal TriangulatedCopy; SurfaceSpline.of(tracer, edgeMesh) snaps the traced ring onto the ORIGINAL mesh's edges through a new ConformingLoopSnap.snap(traceMesh, edgeMesh, path): crossings collapse to the nearer end of the copy edge they cross (a diagonal's ends are quad corners), consecutive vertices are joined by the bounded Dijkstra walk over the original mesh's edges only, and dead-end spurs are pruned so the mask is one closed loop (pruning runs only when the two meshes differ, so triangle meshes and fertility_rings are untouched). The editing scene keeps the triangle copy for picking/tracing; RingScene.ringMaskSurface() gives the original, and the tool's draft and adopted rings snap onto it, so tool and graph masks agree. A diagonal step on a quad costs two quad edges: a tilted ring on the 16-around tube marks 38 edges (a level ring 16-23), on the 12-around finger 18 (level 12).

Verified 2026-10-03 (rework): QuadRingToolTest 4/4 (level and tilted spline_ring on a procedural quad cylinder: face count and arity preserved, edge count unchanged, mask only quad edges, every marked vertex degree 2, one loop, tool fingerprint == saved statement fingerprint, RingRegions on the quad mesh with the mask gives 2 regions); mvn test 380 run, 0 failures; wt done build + launch OK. In app on tmp copies: quad tube drafted tilted ring (2 authored anchors), confirmed, Ctrl+S, relaunch: graph output 1280 faces/2544 edges (quads), ring_00 38 edges fingerprint ed839058a88dc8b6 in both the graph marks and the tool's reloaded ring; Ctrl+T split into 2 regions and selected one. Quad finger: 288 faces kept, 18 edges, fingerprint b9af6d63ebe8b38a in graph and tool after reload; region tool 2 regions. fertility_rings.dsl unchanged (md5 0563edc0...), loads 13 rings, graph/tool fingerprints all agree. Screenshots tmp/craw39r-tube-{draft,confirmed,reloaded,regions}.png, tmp/craw39r-finger-{draft,confirmed,reloaded,regions}.png, tmp/craw39r-fertility.png.

Merge onto master with CRAW-37 (2026-10-03): ixd wt sync conflicted only in SplineRingNode's geometry socket doc and the generated mesh-node-catalog.json (docs merged: input mesh passes through unchanged, marks on its own edges, traced spline in _surface_splines); evaluate, SurfaceSpline, RingTool and RingScene merged cleanly and spline_ring puts SurfaceSpline.of(ring.tracer, mesh) in the slot. SurfaceSpline.mesh now means the triangle surface the spline was traced on (what pointVertexId/pointEdgeId/pointFraction index: the mesh itself, or its TriangulatedCopy); new SurfaceSpline.edgeMesh is the mesh markedByEdgeId indexes; inBundle matches on edgeMesh == bundle.mesh(). Quad cut-out: RingRegionExtraction.build() cuts on cutSurface = TriangulatedCopy.of(regions.mesh) (the same deterministic copy spline_ring and the scene trace on; identity for triangle meshes), maps each copy triangle to its source face with the new TriangulatedCopy.sourceActiveFaceByActiveFace for region labels (parentActiveFaceByTriangle indexes the regions' faces), accepts a spline when spline.mesh == cutSurface or spline.edgeMesh == regions.mesh, and measures meanEdgeLength on the regions' own edges. The extracted mesh is all triangles, also from quads. Verified: QuadRingToolTest 5/5 incl. new aRegionCutFromAQuadCylinderAlongASplineRingIsAClosedSolid (tilted spline_ring on the procedural quad cylinder -> extract_ring_region bottom: 16 crossings, boundary to spline 0.0000 vs snapped loop 0.421, 1 loop capped, closed=true, Manifold NO_ERROR, source keeps its quads); RingRegionExtractionTest 3/3; mvn test 384 run, 0 failures. RingRegionExtractionBenchmark on a fertility copy identical to CRAW-37: region 2 boundary 0.1094 vs snapped 1.2638, 3432 faces closed NO_ERROR; region 4 0.0825 vs 1.3514; union 14410 faces volume 178090.5 NO_ERROR (the benchmark needs a two-ring tube region, so it does not apply to the one-ring quad tube). Scene, fertility copy: region 9 E -> 2614 faces, boundary 0.0559 vs snapped 1.1272, closed NO_ERROR (CRAW-37: 0.056/1.127/2614). Scene, quad tube copy (tmp/quad_tube.dsl): Ctrl+T 2 regions, picked region 1, E -> 47 crossings, boundary 0.0024 vs snapped 0.0898, capped 1/1, 1116 triangles, closed=true NO_ERROR; O shows the open cut on the spline. fertility_rings.dsl unchanged (md5 0563edc0). wt done green. Screenshots tmp/craw39m-tube-{regions,selected,extracted,open-cut}.png, tmp/craw39m-fertility-{regions,selected,extracted}.png.

Rework 3 (2026-10-03): TriangulatedCopy is gone; quads are handled inside the intrinsic layer. IntrinsicTriangulation.buildConnectivity now ear-clips every polygon into intrinsic triangles, each step cutting the shortest diagonal of an ear valid in the polygon's Newell plane (a convex quad splits on its shorter diagonal; ear-split rather than fanned so a concave polygon never folds over itself and a 16-gon cap gets no sliver fan). Split edges take edge indices after the source edges, sourceEdgeId NONE, lengths from source positions; sourceFaceId maps every intrinsic triangle to its polygon; FlipOut flips them like any intrinsic edge. Inside-face point: TracedSurfacePath/SurfaceGeodesics/SurfaceSplineTracer/SurfaceSpline gain a faceId per point (vertexId = edgeId = fraction = -1) located by its surface xyz (TracedSurfacePath.surfacePositions, SurfaceSplineTracer.segmentSurfaceXyz, SurfaceSpline.surfacePolyline); IntrinsicPathTracer emits one where a walk crosses a split edge (face from the snapshot's halfEdgeFace -> sourceFaceId), an unflipped split edge stays a straight corner-to-corner chord. ConformingLoopSnap (one mesh again) snaps an inside point to its polygon's nearest corner and, on a mesh with polygons, prunes dead-end spurs, so masks mark source edges only. RingRegionExtraction cuts the user's own faces: an inside point becomes a cut vertex in its face (or merges into a corner within snapFraction mean edges), a span through inside points is one chord polyline from boundary to boundary that splits the polygon, pieces are triangulated as before (the extracted mesh is triangles; uncut quads are triangulated too, the source keeps its quads). SurfacePicker fans polygons, LineSet.pathStep takes face ids, LimbAxis triangulates a mixed mesh for its skeleton. Deleted: TriangulatedCopy (153 lines), RingScene.halfEdgeSurface override with markedSurface/ringMaskSurface, SurfaceSpline.edgeMesh and of(tracer, edgeMesh), ConformingLoopSnap.snap(traceMesh, edgeMesh, path), RingRegionExtraction.cutSurface and its triangle-to-source-face map.

Verified 2026-10-03 (rework 3): QuadRingToolTest 7/7 incl. new aGeodesicOnAQuadGridIsTheStraightLineThroughItsQuads (7x5 unit quad grid, (1,1)->(6,4) geodesic length = sqrt(34) to 1e-9, every traced point on the line, inside-face points inside their quads; sourceFaceId covers every intrinsic triangle, n-2 per n-gon), theIntrinsicTriangulationSplitsEachPolygonOfTheQuadCylinder (16-gon caps ear-split, cap diameter geodesic = 2.0), aQuadSplitsOnItsShorterDiagonal; the quad-cylinder spline_ring cut reports inside-polygon vertices, closed=true, manifold NO_ERROR. RingRegionExtractionTest 3/3, SurfaceSplineTest 9/9, mvn test 386 run, 0 failures. Fertility (tmp/fertility_rings_copy.dsl; fixture md5 0563edc0... unchanged): 13 rings, graph marks and tool rings identical to the pre-rework run; RingRegionExtractionBenchmark output identical to CRAW-37 apart from timings: region 2 boundary to spline 0.1094 vs snapped 1.2638, 3432 faces closed NO_ERROR; region 4 0.0825; union 14410 faces volume 178090.5 NO_ERROR. Quad tube (tmp/r3_quad_tube.dsl): drafted a tilted ring (2 authored anchors), Enter, Ctrl+S, relaunch: graph output 1280 faces/2544 edges, ring_00 38 edges fingerprint a72951b7cd92fec2 in graph marks and tool; Ctrl+T 2 regions, picked region 1, E: 24 crossings, 21 inserted, 17 vertices inside polygons, boundary to spline 0.0000 vs snapped 0.0808, 1120 faces, closed=true NO_ERROR. Quad finger (tmp/r3_quad_finger.dsl): 288 faces/576 edges kept, ring_00 22 edges fingerprint 62cc7179dcf3751b before and after relaunch; E: 11 crossings, 8 inside, boundary 0.0073 vs snapped 0.1362, 458 faces closed NO_ERROR. wt done green. Screenshots tmp/r3-tube-{load,draft,draft-zoom,confirmed,reloaded,regions,selected,extracted,open-cut}.png, tmp/r3-finger-{load,draft,confirmed,reloaded,regions,selected,extracted}.png, tmp/r3-fertility.png. Known, not from this change: the finger copy's ring overlay is hidden behind its surface from both sides (as in the earlier screenshots); FlipOut leaves a path that hugs the mesh boundary unshortened, on triangles as on quads.
